blocks.text: Illustration of the white dunes and freshwater lagoons of Lençóis Maranhenses

This itinerary shows you several sides of Brazil. In Rio, golden beaches sit alongside granite peaks and the city's best-known landmarks. The Pantanal is one of the richest ecosystems on Earth. In Bonito, you'll find clear rivers, caves and waterfalls. Manaus is your starting point for exploring the Amazon. From São Luís and Barreirinhas, the journey takes in colonial architecture, the ocean and the white dunes of Lençóis Maranhenses.

The Pantanal is considered the world's largest wetland and one of its most diverse ecosystems. Here you can watch birds, capybaras, crocodilians and other wildlife in their natural habitat.

Bonito lies in the southern Pantanal. Much of the landscape remains in its natural state. Old-growth forests surround caves, waterfalls and rivers clear enough to see the life beneath the surface.

The Amazon region covers the Amazon River basin in northern Brazil and stretches from the heights of the Andes to the Atlantic Ocean. You'll begin exploring it from Manaus.

The final leg of the itinerary takes you through São Luís and Barreirinhas. From here, it's easy to reach Lençóis Maranhenses National Park, where seasonal blue and turquoise lagoons form among white sand dunes up to 40 metres high.
